newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African futures exchange slashes trading fees.
newsitem.headline: S.African futures exchange slashes trading fees.

text.p: The South African Futures Exchange (Safex) said on Friday it had approved the reduction of trading fees by around 50 percent.

Part of the reduction is technical in that the executive committee has decided to remove the fee on trades allocated by way of so called "give up" or an allocation of a number of futures or options that have been accumulated in the market in fulfilment of an order.
Aside from this, the fees on index futures, which comprise over 90 percent of Safex trade, will be reduced from 1.70 rand per contract to 1.00 and options from 70 cents to 50 cents.
Together with the removal of the fee on allocations, this will reduce the average fee per contract by 52 percent in the case of futures and 40 percent in the case of options.
The fees for all other financial futures and options including those based on bonds, short-term interest rates and the rand/dollar rate are also to be halved.
Chairman Mark Barnes said Safex had built up reserves to a very sound level and could now afford to reduce the rate of increase in its bank balance.
